transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-16 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Rajiv Patel (CTO - SynTerra), Elena Morales (Head of ML), Sophie Turner (PM), Mark Li (Infra)

Summary (auto): Discussed POC scope to evaluate open models for SynTerra's clinical QA assistant. Focus on benchmarks (latency, accuracy on clinical prompts, multilingual), capacity sizing, and deployment constraints (VPC/KMS).

Shared artifacts: benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.app/synterra/benchmarks), security pack (link: https://redwood.app/synterra/security-pack), sample eval set placeholder (drive link).

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll do a quick intros then jump into the POC goals.
[00:10] Rajiv Patel: hi, Rajiv here, CTO. We're excited to see what open models can do for our triage assistant. Major constraints are accuracy on clinical notes, PII handling, and spanish/french support.
[00:20] Elena Morales: and we also need reproducible latency numbers — the product team's targeting sub-300ms p95/p99-ish for single-turn question answering, ideally.
[00:30] Diego Alvarez: cool, thanks. quick question on workload: what's a typical request look like (tokens in and out) and roughly qps?
[00:40] Sophie Turner: average prompt is ~120 tokens, responses around 140 tokens; peak concurrency expected 30-50 qps during business hours, steady 8-12 qps. Monthly active callers maybe 200k.
[01:00] Priya Rao: ok that's helpful. for POC we usually run bench with representative set — will you be able to provide 200-500 sample prompts including multilingual and edge clinical cases?
[01:10] Elena Morales: yes we can do 500, will include spanish/french and a subset of notes with redactions.
[01:20] Mark Li: infra constraints — we need VPC peering for Dedicated or Private, and KMS for key management, can't have logs leaving our account for certain datasets.
[01:30] Maya Chen: got it, we'll include security checklist. now model selection — Diego, want to run through the open-model shortlist and the tradeoffs?
[01:40] Diego Alvarez: yeah. given your needs I'd recommend starting with three families: Mistral 7B Chat / 8x2 variants for cost-latency balance, Llama 2 13B for stronger instruction-following and community finetunes, and Falcon 40B Instruct as a higher-quality candidate for clinical text. also mention RedPajama / MPT variants if you want lower-cost but we expect lower clinical accuracy. each has tradeoffs: smaller models like Mistral are cheaper and faster (lower CPU/GPU footprint) but may need more prompt engineering for domain accuracy. larger models give better zero-shot QA but higher cost and latency.
[02:10] Rajiv Patel: is there data on multilingual capability? we need spanish first, french next.
[02:20] Diego Alvarez: Mistral tends to be strongest on English; Llama 2 13B has decent multilingual backbone, Falcon 40B also covers many languages better, but real accuracy depends on finetuning. we recommended including prompt/finetune eval for spanish clinical examples.
[02:40] Elena Morales: fine-tuning vs retrieval-augmented generation? we plan to use RAG over our knowledge base for factuality, so model hallucination tolerance is important.
[02:50] Priya Rao: for RAG setups, smaller models often do fine when the context is good. But for subtle clinical reasoning you might prefer the larger Falcon or a finetuned Llama. During POC we can test both RAG + finetune prototypes.
[03:10] Sophie Turner: timeline wise what do you suggest for a POC? we want a decision point to pick a model for pilot by mid-April.
[03:20] Maya Chen: typical POC is 4-6 weeks: week 1 — ingest samples + baseline runs, week 2 — focused benchmarks for latency and quality, week 3 — RAG/finetune experiments, week 4 — security review + final recommendations. can extend for deeper finetune.
[03:40] Mark Li: and for Dedicated vs Hosted — if we need VPC and KMS we likely need Dedicated or Private. what's the difference in latency/cost?
[03:50] Diego Alvarez: Dedicated gives reserved GPUs and predictable throughput; latency similar to hosted but with isolation and VPC peering. cost-wise Dedicated has commit pricing but can be more economical at scale. Private on-prem is heavier to set up but meets strict compliance. we'll provide a cost model for expected qps.
[04:10] Rajiv Patel: what's the benchmark plan specifically? we need both quality (F1/EM on QA sets) and latency distribution.
[04:20] Priya Rao: we'll run per-model baseline: single-instance latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput with batching profiles, and quality metrics on your labelled set (exact match, F1, and human ratings for clinical correctness). also measure token cost per response.
[04:40] Elena Morales: for acceptance criteria: p95 latency < 300ms on typical prompt length, EM/F1 within 5% of our internal golden baseline, and no critical hallucination on a 50-case spot check.
[05:00] Diego Alvarez: noted. for GPU sizing: with your token lengths and 30-50 peak qps, rough estimate — Mistral 7B on one A10/NVIDIA instance could handle X qps with batching, Llama 13B needs bigger instance and more memory; Falcon 40B likely requires A100-class or multi-GPU. we'll quantify exact instance types in the follow-up.
[05:30] Sophie Turner: cost target? we can't exceed current budget for LLM infra by more than 2x for the pilot.
[05:40] Maya Chen: understood. we'll model per-token costs and show tradeoffs for latency/cost/quality so you can pick the best fit.
[06:00] Rajiv Patel: any major red flags on data residency / logs? we can't ship PII to hosted logs.
[06:10] Maya Chen: we have options: redact before sending, bring-your-own-key with KMS, and Dedicated/Private where logs remain in your VPC. we'll include redaction best practices in the security pack.
[06:30] Elena Morales: curious about quantization — will 4-bit quantized versions keep enough quality for clinical QA?
[06:40] Diego Alvarez: often 4-bit quant can be very good for many tasks, but for clinical precision it's model dependent. part of the POC will test fp16 vs quantized variants to measure quality regression.
[06:55] Mark Li: network — we'll provide peering and a load balancer; can you support mTLS and SAML?
[07:05] Priya Rao: yes, Redwood supports mTLS + SAML SSO; we'll document required flows.
[07:15] Sophie Turner: ok let's recap the shortlist: Mistral 7B chat (fast/cost-efficient), Llama 2 13B (balanced, good community finetunes), Falcon 40B Instruct (higher quality for clinical text). add a wild-card like RedPajama or commercial OpenAI model if needed for comparison.
[07:35] Diego Alvarez: we'll also include quantized variants for each where possible and baseline the RAG vs finetune approaches.
[07:45] Rajiv Patel: what about eval for multilingual? will you run spanish/french prompts?
[07:50] Priya Rao: yes, include multilingual subset and human raters for a sample. we'll also surface per-language metrics.
[08:00] Maya Chen: next steps — we'll send the benchmark spreadsheet, proposed instance sizing, and a draft POC schedule. SynTerra to send sample prompts and confirm security constraints.
[08:10] Elena Morales: confirm. I'll upload samples and label the expected answers.
[08:20] Mark Li: I'll send network diagram and list of compliance requirements.
[08:30] Sophie Turner: can we get a tentative cost estimate before the next checkpoint?
[08:35] Maya Chen: yes, Diego will include cost estimates for hosted vs dedicated for each model.
[08:45] (crosstalk, brief)
[09:00] Maya Chen: ok thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the perf run for the week of 2026-03-23.
[09:10] Rajiv Patel: thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
